historical_growth.growth_rate_source: forward blend of FY2026 guidance (organic Service up mid-to-high single digits on ~65% of sales; New Equipment down low single digits to flat) decelerating toward terminal; equity CAGR unusable because book equity has been negative since the April-2020 spin (-5,748 at Jun-26), so revenue and owner-FCF CAGRs anchor the check
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR not computable (negative book value since spin-off). EPS 5yr CAGR 11.0% is far above revenue 2.5% and owner-FCF 2.0%: the gap is buybacks (diluted shares 434.6M FY2020 -> 394.9M FY2025, -1.9%/yr) and margin, not volume. FY2024 EPS ($4.10) also carries a ~$185M one-off German tax benefit, so the 3yr EPS CAGR is measured FY2022->FY2025 to avoid it.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC): FY2020 1,234 -> FY2025 1,364 (2.0%/yr); FY2022 1,378 -> FY2025 1,364 (-0.3%/yr). Reported FCF: FY2020 1,297 -> FY2025 1,444 (2.2%); FY2022 1,445 -> FY2025 1,444 (0.0%). SBC grew 63 -> 80 over the same five years (4.9%/yr), faster than FCF, so a slightly rising share of reported growth is being paid in stock, though at 0.5% of revenue it is immaterial. Revenue FY2020 12,756 -> FY2025 14,431 (2.5%); FY2022 13,685 -> FY2025 14,431 (1.8%). EPS FY2020 2.09 -> FY2025 3.52 (11.0%); FY2022 2.98 -> FY2025 3.52 (5.7%).

scenario_narratives.base: Service-led model holds: Service organic growth mid-single digits on the 2.5M-unit portfolio with modernization (backlog +26% cc) and repair growing double digits; New Equipment flat as Americas/EMEA growth offsets structural decline in China (high-teens declines, ~10% of sales now vs ~20% pre-2022). The 2026 margin trough (adj OP 15.3% in H1-26, -160bp) recovers to the FY2025 level by 2032 as the service-quality and pricing investments mature. CEO succession by Jul-2027 is orderly. Base-case value is close to the current price: the 2026 de-rating (52w range 63.6-94.6) has already removed the premium, and Otis now trades near a fully-SBC-expensed owner-FCF value at an 8% WACC.
scenario_narratives.bull: China new-equipment orders bottom in 2027, the aging installed base in the Americas and EMEA drives a multi-year modernization cycle, and the 2026 investment in service quality and pricing capability returns Otis to its historical ~50bp/yr margin expansion, taking pre-SBC EBITDA margin to 19.5% by 2032 with revenue growing 5-5.5% near term. The stock re-rates back toward a 20x FCF compounder multiple.
scenario_narratives.bear: China's new-equipment decline continues and feeds through to a shrinking China service book; maintenance price increases fail to cover mechanic wage inflation and material costs; the 2026 initiatives become permanent spend and margins settle 150-200bp below FY2025. Revenue grows 1-2% and the incoming CEO resets expectations. Net debt of $7.6B (about 2.9x FY2026E EBITDA) is serviceable but caps buybacks; the terminal multiple compresses to 14x. No solvency risk in this path.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Otis is valued as a service annuity with a cyclical, low-margin new-equipment front end. Value is driven almost entirely by the maintenance/modernization/repair stream (~90% of segment profit) and its margin trajectory; new equipment matters as a feeder of future service units, not as a profit source. House basis expenses SBC fully and holds the share count flat, so the ~$1.6B/yr buyback is value-neutral rather than a source of per-share growth. NCI is deducted once in the bridge at an earnings multiple; leases are charged in the flows; pension is left in the flows via contributions. Risk is charged once, in the driver paths and the 25/50/25 weights, not in a scenario-varying WACC.
key_risks_to_valuation: China new equipment (roughly 10% of sales, formerly ~20%) continues to decline and the China service portfolio follows with a lag
2026 service-quality/pricing/digital investments become a permanent cost base: adj OP margin stays at ~15% instead of recovering to 16.5-17%
Mechanic labour inflation outpaces maintenance pricing in the Americas and EMEA
CEO succession (Judy Marks retiring by 31-Jul-2027) brings a strategy or guidance reset
Net debt $7.6B (~2.9x FY2026E EBITDA) at rising refinancing coupons (new notes >5% vs 3.2% average); interest expense already up ~$10M/qtr y/y
Terminal value is ~60% of EV and the 18x cap binds: value is sensitive to the exit multiple a buyer grants a 2.5%-growth annuity
Residual Separation tax exposures under the Tax Matters Agreement with RTX/Carrier

sanity_check_review.result: tripped on one rule (implied P/B -5.24x vs 1.5x the 10yr max of -6.40x); trip judged INAPPLICABLE, no fix applied
reasoning: Book equity has been negative since the April-2020 spin from UTC (-5,748 at 2026-06-30, after 5,005 of treasury stock), so P/B is undefined as a valuation multiple and the rule compares two negative numbers: a less-negative implied P/B is not a richer valuation. The P/B rule is excluded for negative-equity companies.

Every multiple that does apply says the model is conservative, not rich: implied P/E 20.6x (SBC-adjusted) is below the 10yr minimum of 24.5x and the average of 26.8x; implied P/Sales 1.96x is below the 10yr minimum of 2.30x; EV/EBITDA could not be evaluated because the CSV carries no EBITDA column (implied terminal EV/EBITDA 11.8x in the JSON vs ~12.6x on the current price).

Diagnosis 'growth_too_high' (3.5% selected vs 1.6% through-cycle revenue CAGR): the 2018-2025 CAGR spans COVID and a four-year China new-equipment collapse; FY2026 guidance alone is +5% and Service (65% of sales) grew 7-9% organically in H1-26. Base growth already fades from 4% to 2.5% over the horizon and the bear case (25% weight) runs 1-2%. Not changed.

Diagnosis 'wacc_too_low' (cyclicality keyword): cyclicality is charged in the driver paths and the 25% bear weight; adding a WACC premium would charge it twice (adaptations rule f). WACC 8.0% is built from USD rf 4.2% + 5% ERP at beta ~1.0, 24% debt weight. Not changed.

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 380.67M cover-page shares at 2026-07-15 (Q2-26 10-Q, dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding) plus ~0.9M dilutive awards (Q2-26 diluted 383.5M less basic 382.6M). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would double-charge. The ~$1.6B/yr buyback pace (H1-26 $807M) is the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat and is value-neutral in this model.
inputs.net_debt_note: 2026-06-30 10-Q: long-term debt 8,226 (7,046 non-current + 1,180 current portion) + other short-term borrowings 210 = 8,436; cash 813. The Metrics.csv TotalDebt of 9,616 double-counts the current portion (adds DebtCurrent 1,390 on top of LongTermDebt 8,226 which already includes 1,180). Operating lease liabilities (~580 incl. current) EXCLUDED: ASC 842 operating lease cost sits in operating profit and OCF, so the lease is charged in the flows (treatment B). Unfunded pension/OPEB of 411 is not added as debt because service cost and ~$43M/yr contributions already run through the flows. German tax refund receivable (35 tax + 20 interest) nets against the 55 payable to RTX under the TMA, so it is ignored.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement, 'Stock compensation cost' add-back $80M (XBRL ShareBasedCompensation). Otis publishes no combined equity-award figure and does not tag withholding taxes on net-share settlement separately ('Other financing activities, net' is +$6M in H1-26), so the add-back alone is used; the understatement is immaterial at 0.5% of revenue.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing-activity repurchases $809M; FY2024 $1,007M; H1-26 $807M (annualising ~$1.6B). Dividends FY2025 $647M.
inputs.fy0_note: FY0 is the current guidance year (Dec-26 year end), anchored to the 2026-07-22 revised outlook: net sales $15.1-15.3B (midpoint 15,200 used), adjusted operating profit ~$2.4B, adjusted EPS $4.01-4.05, adjusted FCF $1.50-1.55B. FY2025 actual revenue was 14,431 and H1-26 was 7,425 (+7%). Year 1 of the projection is FY2027.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate: risk-free ~4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.0 for a global capital-goods/service annuity -> cost of equity ~9.2%; pre-tax marginal cost of debt ~5% (weighted-average coupon 3.2% on existing notes, new 2026 issuance higher), ~3.8% after tax; net debt ~24% of enterprise value -> WACC 0.76x9.2 + 0.24x3.8 = 7.9%, rounded to 8.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality, China and the CEO transition are priced in the driver paths and the weights, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: B (leases as operating cost). ASC 842 operating lease expense (~$150M/yr; ROU assets 580) is inside operating profit and OCF, so it is already deducted in EBITDA; lease liabilities are therefore excluded from net debt. Finance leases (~$6M) are inside long-term debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are whole-company; the noncontrolling interest is deducted ONCE in the equity bridge at -800 (approx. 12.5x the ~$65M/yr attributable to NCI: FY2025 $71M GAAP / ~$60M adjusted, H1-26 $34M / $23M adjusted). Book NCI is only 294 (188 + 106 redeemable) but Otis has been buying these stakes out at multiples of book (Otis Electric China 2025, $215M redemption Oct-25), so an earnings-based value is the honest deduction. Leakage is shrinking as stakes are acquired; it is not folded into the tax rate.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md: operating company, US industrial with a cyclical new-equipment segment and a recurring service annuity). First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. owner_fcf FY2025 = reported FCF 1,444 - SBC 80 - interest income 0 = 1,364 (net debt company: interest income NOT stripped). SBC is 0.55% of revenue, so the house/street band is narrow. FY0 revenue is the guidance midpoint; the FY0 EBITDA margin of 17.2% is built from guidance: adjusted operating profit 2,400 less ~40 of recurring 'other restructuring' (an owner's cost that recurs every year: 18 in H1-26, 35 in H1-25) plus D&A ~170 plus SBC ~80 = ~2,610 / 15,200. Cash tax 25% on unlevered EBIT (adjusted ETR 24.7% H1-26, 23-25% recent; cash taxes paid FY2025 471 on pretax 1,934). Capex driver 1.6% = 1.1% PP&E capex (FY2025 152, FY2024 126, H1-26 77) + ~0.5% of revenue for the bolt-on service-provider acquisitions (FY2025 109, H1-26 193) that feed the service-portfolio growth being projected. Working capital capture 0%: Otis runs negative working capital (contract liabilities 3,023) but historical OCF conversion shows a mild drag, not a tailwind. Sanity: FY0 unlevered owner FCF of ~1,700 reconciles to the $1.50-1.55B adjusted FCF guidance plus ~$170M after-tax cash interest less ~$50M restructuring/bolt-on cash. Share-count basis: count held flat because SBC is expensed; buybacks are value-neutral. Price is a regular-session close, not after-hours.

bear.narrative: China new equipment keeps falling and the shrinking installed-base additions start to show in the China service portfolio; Western maintenance pricing cannot outrun mechanic wage inflation; the 2026 investment spend becomes a permanent cost base rather than a one-year dip, so the pre-SBC EBITDA margin settles at 16% (adj OP ~14.3%). FY2026 guidance has already been cut once (from +$60-100M to flat/-$30M adjusted operating profit); a new CEO in 2027 resets it again. Terminal 14x for an ex-growth industrial.

base.growth_rationale: Service (~65% of sales, ~90% of segment profit) grows mid-single digits on an aging 2.5M-unit portfolio, modernization backlog +26% cc and repair demand; New Equipment flat-to-down as China (high-teens declines in orders and sales through Q2-26) keeps shrinking while the Americas grow. Blended ~4% fading to 2.5%.
base.margin_rationale: FY2026 is an investment trough (adj op margin 15.3% H1-26 vs 16.9% H1-25: service-quality, pricing and digital initiatives, labour and material cost, China NE price). Base recovers only ~130bp over six years to 18.5% pre-SBC EBITDA, i.e. back to the FY2025 level of ~18.4% (adj OP 16.6% + D&A 1.2% + SBC 0.55%), not beyond it. Cap 18x: Gordon at 8%/2.5% is 18.6x so the cap binds marginally.
base.narrative: Service annuity compounds; New Equipment is a drag that stops mattering. CEO succession (Marks retires by Jul-27) is executed without strategy change.

bull.narrative: China new equipment bottoms in 2027 and the Americas/EMEA modernization cycle (backlog +26%) carries Service growth at high single digits; the 2026 service-quality and pricing investments deliver the ~50bp/yr margin expansion Otis produced pre-2026, taking the pre-SBC EBITDA margin to 19.5% by 2032. Buybacks continue at ~$1.5B/yr (value-neutral here, but they are the mechanism). Terminal 20x: a recurring-revenue compounder re-rates toward its pre-2026 multiple.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25% because the two headline negatives are structural, not cyclical: China new equipment has declined for four years with no sign of a floor (orders down high teens in Q2-26), and the 2026 margin compression is the company's own investment choice whose payback is unproven; a CEO change in 2027 adds reset risk. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things to go right at once (China bottoms, modernization cycle sustains, margins re-expand). Base 50%: the service annuity is intact (Service organic +9% in Q2-26, the best since spin) and that is most of the value.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
